in.wrong: I like very much pizza.
in.right: I like pizza very much.

in.right: It depends on the weather.

en.tip: The verb “depend” always goes with “on”, never “of”.

in.wrong: We discuss about the plan.

native.comment: Resposta: “have”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “I live here since”?
en.tip: With “since” we use the present perfect: “I have lived”, not “I live”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I live here since 2020.” The right way is “I have lived here since 2020.” Many learners use the present here, but English needs the present perfect. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: She gave me many informations.
in.right: She gave me a lot of information.

native.comment: Resposta: “information”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Information” has no plural in English. Say “a lot of information”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She gave me many informations.” The right way is “She gave me a lot of information.” The plural “informações” feels natural, but English does not allow the s. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

native.comment: Resposta: “bookstore”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Library” means a place to borrow books. A shop is a “bookstore”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I bought a book at the library.” The right way is “I bought a book at the bookstore.” This false friend confuses many learners. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I am very exciting about the trip.
in.right: I am very excited about the trip.
in.why: I feel excited. A trip is exciting.

native.tip: Para sentimentos usamos “-ed”: “excited”. Para coisas, “-ing”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am very exciting about the trip.” O certo é “I am very excited about the trip.” Quem sente é “excited”; o que causa a emoção é “exciting”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “excited”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: For feelings we use “-ed”: “excited”. For things, “-ing”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I am very exciting about the trip.” The right way is “I am very excited about the trip.” The person who feels is “excited”; the thing that causes it is “exciting”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: My cousin is married with a doctor.
in.right: My cousin is married to a doctor.
in.answer_say: To! She is married to my brother.

native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “My cousin is married with a doctor.” O certo é “My cousin is married to a doctor.” O “com” do português não vira “with” aqui. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “to”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, “casado com” is “married to”.

in.wrong: I am agree with you.
in.right: I agree with you.
in.answer_say: Agree! I agree with you.

native.tip: “Agree” já é verbo. Não use “am” antes dele.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I am agree with you.” O certo é “I agree with you.” Em português é “estou de acordo”, mas em inglês é só “agree”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “agree”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: “Agree” is already a verb. Do not put “am” before it.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I am agree with you.” The right way is “I agree with you.” Learners think of “estou de acordo”, but in English it is just “agree”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: It has a lot of people here.
in.right: There are a lot of people here.
in.why: To say something exists, use there is or there are.
in.answer_say: There are! There are many people here.

native.tip: Para dizer que existe algo, use “there is” ou “there are”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “It has a lot of people here.” O certo é “There are a lot of people here.” O verbo “ter” do português tem dois usos; em inglês são dois verbos. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “There are”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: To say that something exists, use “there is” or “there are”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “It has a lot of people here.” The right way is “There are a lot of people here.” The verb “ter” has two uses; English uses two different verbs. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Is cold today.
in.right: It is cold today.
in.answer_say: It! It is hot today.

native.tip: Em inglês, a frase precisa de sujeito: “It is cold”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “Is cold today.” O certo é “It is cold today.” Em português dizemos “está frio”, sem sujeito. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “It”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In English, the sentence needs a subject: “It is cold”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Is cold today.” The right way is “It is cold today.” Learners say “está frio” with no subject, but English needs one. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I go to home after work.
in.right: I go home after work.
in.answer_say: Go! I want to go home.

native.tip: Com “home”, não usamos “to”: “go home”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I go to home after work.” O certo é “I go home after work.” Home é uma exceção que vale decorar. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “go”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: With “home”, we do not use “to”: “go home”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I go to home after work.” The right way is “I go home after work.” Home is an exception worth remembering. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: She don't like coffee.
in.right: She doesn't like coffee.
in.answer_say: Doesn't! He doesn't like tea.

native.tip: Com “he”, “she” e “it” usamos “doesn't”.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “She don't like coffee.” O certo é “She doesn't like coffee.” Em português o verbo muda na terminação, mas em inglês “she” pede “doesn't”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “doesn't”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: With “he”, “she” and “it” we use “doesn't”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “She don't like coffee.” The right way is “She doesn't like coffee.” In their own language the verb ending changes, but in English “she” needs “doesn't”. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I need to make my homework.
in.right: I need to do my homework.
in.answer_say: Do! I always do my homework.

native.tip: Tarefa de casa é “do homework”. Em português usamos “fazer” para tudo.
native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I need to make my homework.” O certo é “I need to do my homework.” Em inglês, “fazer” se divide em “make” e “do”. Ouça a Ama e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “do”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: Homework is “do homework”. In Portuguese we use “do” for everything.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I need to make my homework.” The right way is “I need to do my homework.” In English, “fazer” splits into “make” and “do”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I will call you when I will arrive.
in.right: I will call you when I arrive.
in.answer_say: Arrive! Call me when you arrive.

native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I will call you when I will arrive.” O certo é “I will call you when I arrive.” Em português usamos o futuro do subjuntivo (“quando eu chegar”), mas em inglês vem o presente. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.
native.comment: Resposta: “arrive”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.hook: Do you say “when I will arrive”?

en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I will call you when I will arrive.” The right way is “I will call you when I arrive.” Learners use a future form (“quando eu chegar”), but English uses the present. Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: Where you live?

native.comment: Resposta: “do”. Treine mais com um quiz grátis aqui: {link}

en.tip: In questions, we need the helper “do” or “does”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “Where you live?” The right way is “Where do you live?” Learners think the tone is enough, but English needs “do”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.

in.wrong: I want that you help me.

native.caption: Cuidado com este erro comum! 😬 Muita gente diz “I want that you help me.” O certo é “I want you to help me.” Em português usamos “quero que você”. Ouça o Carlos e repita! Treine mais no app Lexkite.

en.hook: Do you say “I want that you”?

in.wrong: Can you borrow me a pen?
